input_needed: pincode or full dataset download; free API key for API use
what_it_returns: Circle, region, division, office name, PIN code, office type, delivery status, district, state.
why_it_matters: Turns a PIN into district/state/region. This is the cleanest public baseline for Indian geography in this project.
remarks: India's official government PIN-code master list. The most trustworthy way to check a PIN is real and to map it to district/state. Download the whole file once and keep it local for instant offline lookups.

what_it_returns: Post offices for that PIN, district, state, circle, region, delivery status.
why_it_matters: Fast no-key prototype lookup for PIN→district/state. Good for learning and spot checks.
remarks: A quick, no-signup way to turn a PIN into district/state/post-office. It mirrors India Post data, so for anything serious cross-check against the official Data.gov.in file.

source: India Post PIN search / DIGIPIN references
input_needed: PIN, post office, or future DIGIPIN if available in bank records
what_it_returns: Manual PIN/post-office lookup; future precise grid-style digital addressing where available.
why_it_matters: Official manual fallback when APIs disagree or fail. DIGIPIN could become useful later if banks capture it.
remarks: Official India Post PIN search. DIGIPIN is India Post's newer grid-based 'digital PIN' that can pinpoint a small area — worth watching, used only where available.

input_needed: place text, city/state, PIN, or coordinates
what_it_returns: Latitude/longitude and structured place data from OpenStreetMap.
why_it_matters: Converts a place/PIN/city into map coordinates for later distance/region work.
remarks: Free address->coordinates (and back). Great for demos, but the public server allows only ~1 request/second, needs a real app name in the request, and you must cache results. For volume, self-host or use a paid geocoder.

input_needed: place text, address, PIN, API key
what_it_returns: Lat/lon, formatted address, state/city/postcode, confidence/rank fields.
why_it_matters: More practical than public Nominatim for repeated prototype geocoding.
remarks: A friendlier geocoder with a generous free tier and clean structured output. Good middle option between the free public Nominatim and paid Google.

what_it_returns: Lat/lon, formatted address, components, confidence annotations.
why_it_matters: Good testing geocoder; useful if Nominatim is too limited.
remarks: Geocoder built on open data with worldwide coverage. Free tier is really a trial for testing; ongoing use needs a paid plan.

what_it_returns: High-quality geocoding, place coordinates, formatted address components.
why_it_matters: Enterprise-grade geocoding candidate if a bank accepts cost and Google terms.
remarks: The highest-quality geocoder with excellent India coverage, but it costs money at scale and has usage terms. Use when accuracy really matters; avoid for bulk if budget is tight.

input_needed: area, bounding box, OSM tags such as amenity=bank, highway, railway, bus_station
what_it_returns: Roads, towns, banks, ATMs, transport nodes, POI counts from OpenStreetMap.
why_it_matters: Builds area context: urban density, transport access, banking/ATM density. This is region context, not person lookup.
remarks: Lets you COUNT map features in an area (banks, ATMs, roads, transport). Gives 'how urban/connected is this area' context — never a person's location. Rate-limited; be gentle.

what_it_returns: Bulk offline OSM roads/places/POIs without hitting public APIs.
why_it_matters: Best option for serious offline area-context processing once geospatial skills improve.
remarks: A downloadable copy of all OpenStreetMap data for India. Use it offline so you never hit public rate limits — good once you move past tiny demos.

what_it_returns: Community-maintained India administrative boundary shapefiles/GeoJSON.
why_it_matters: Helps map district/state data and join geospatial data locally.
remarks: Community-maintained India state/district boundary files. Needed to draw maps and to join your data to the right district. Check the licence before any commercial use.

what_it_returns: Population, urban/rural, demographic district-level context.
why_it_matters: Creates regional priors: population weight, urbanity, density. Helps avoid naive “all regions equal” thinking later.
remarks: District-level population and urban/rural figures. Use it to weight areas (busier districts are more likely) so the model doesn't treat every place as equally probable. The latest full census is 2011 — dated but still a useful baseline.

what_it_returns: Indian map layers, imagery, boundaries, thematic geospatial datasets.
why_it_matters: India-specific geospatial reference source for boundaries and area context.
remarks: India's own government map/satellite portal with official boundaries and layers. Can be slow, and some downloads need a free login.

what_it_returns: Administrative boundaries at multiple levels.
why_it_matters: Quick boundary source for personal GIS experiments.
remarks: Ready-made administrative boundary shapes for India at several levels (state/district/sub-district). Free, but its licence restricts commercial redistribution — read it first.

what_it_returns: Country, region/state, city, lat/lon, timezone, ISP, organization, ASN, mobile/proxy/hosting flags.
why_it_matters: Fast no-key way to turn IP into approximate region and trust flags for demos.
remarks: The easiest no-key way to turn an IP into an approximate city + VPN/proxy/mobile flags. Free tier is HTTP-only, ~45 requests/minute, and non-commercial — fine for learning/prototyping, not production.

input_needed: public_ip looked up in local .mmdb file
what_it_returns: Country, subdivision/state, city, postal, lat/lon, accuracy_radius.
why_it_matters: Best local/offline IP location option after download. Accuracy radius makes uncertainty visible.
remarks: A downloadable IP->city database you query offline (no per-call limit). It also gives an 'accuracy radius' so you know how fuzzy each IP guess is. Its licence forbids using it to identify a specific household/individual.

what_it_returns: Country, continent, ASN, AS name, AS domain.
why_it_matters: Useful for network owner/ASN features and country-level sanity check.
remarks: Free IP lookup, but the Lite tier only returns country + the network owner (no Indian city/state). Good for a quick country/VPN sanity check; city-level needs the paid tier.

what_it_returns: Detailed geolocation, privacy/VPN, carrier/mobile, company/ASN fields depending plan.
why_it_matters: Stronger IP intelligence if bank needs vendor-grade enrichments.
remarks: The paid IPinfo tiers add city/region plus explicit VPN/proxy/Tor flags and carrier/company data — a sharper second opinion when IP trust matters.

input_needed: public_ip or local IP range join
what_it_returns: IP range to country/region/city/lat/lon depending edition.
why_it_matters: Alternative local IP geolocation DB if MaxMind is not used.
remarks: A free downloadable IP-to-location database, similar idea to MaxMind GeoLite2. Handy as a cross-check or backup. Fields depend on the edition you download.

input_needed: public_ip or local IP range join
what_it_returns: IP range to country/region/city/lat/lon depending selected DB package.
why_it_matters: Alternative downloadable IP geolocation database.
remarks: Another free offline IP-to-location database. Useful to compare against MaxMind/DB-IP — if two databases disagree a lot, trust the IP less.

input_needed: public_ip or local IP range join
what_it_returns: Proxy/VPN/datacenter type flags depending edition.
why_it_matters: Does not give location; tells whether IP location should be trusted less.
remarks: A companion database that flags whether an IP is a known proxy/VPN/datacentre. Use it to DOWN-WEIGHT an IP's location, not to locate anyone.

what_it_returns: Abuse confidence score, report categories, report history.
why_it_matters: Flags dirty infrastructure that can weaken IP trust.
remarks: A community database of IP 'abuse' reports. Tells you if an IP is widely flagged as malicious — a trust signal about the connection, not a location.

what_it_returns: Parse/validate/format number, country code, possible number type; sometimes carrier metadata via libphonenumber metadata.
why_it_matters: Cleans phone numbers before any telecom-circle or vendor lookup.
remarks: Google's offline number library. It validates an Indian number, says its type, and (via its carrier add-on) hints the original operator. It gives NO live location — only structure.

what_it_returns: Original operator/service area/circle where number series was allocated, if table is available.
why_it_matters: Weak historical region hint from number series. Useful only as tie-breaker.
remarks: Public references for which operator/circle a number-series was originally issued in. Treat as a weak region hint only — number portability and relocation make it stale.

source: Mobile intelligence APIs: DataYuge / Twilio Lookup / Abstract / Numverify
what_it_returns: Validation, carrier, line type, risk/identity signals, maybe coarse location depending vendor/plan.
why_it_matters: Possible phone metadata enrichment if bank approves a vendor.
remarks: Vendor APIs that validate a number and return operator/circle, line type, and risk/identity signals. DataYuge is India-focused (operator+circle+MNP); Twilio/Abstract/Numverify are global. None give live physical location.

what_it_returns: Bank, branch, address, city, district, state, MICR if available.
why_it_matters: Turns IFSC into branch geography. Useful if loan source/disbursement branch is known.
remarks: Free, no-key lookup that turns a branch's IFSC code into the bank, branch, city, district and state. Community data (not RBI-official), so cross-check for production; returns 404 if the IFSC is wrong.

what_it_returns: Official branch/IFSC/MICR lookup output.
why_it_matters: Official reference for branch geography validation.
remarks: The official RBI page to confirm a branch's IFSC/MICR. Authoritative but manual (no clean bulk API) — use it to verify, not to fetch in volume.

input_needed: user permission in browser/app; secure HTTPS context
what_it_returns: Latitude/longitude/accuracy from device/browser where user allows it.
why_it_matters: Potential consented signal during digital journeys.
remarks: Built into browsers/apps: if the user taps 'Allow', it returns their device's lat/long + accuracy. It is consent-based and device-side — not something you can call from a phone number.

source: Google Geolocation API using Wi-Fi/cell data
input_needed: device-side Wi-Fi access points/cell tower observations + API key
what_it_returns: Estimated lat/lon and accuracy radius from cell/Wi-Fi signals.
why_it_matters: Can locate a device when GPS is weak, but only from consented device-side observations.
remarks: Turns nearby Wi-Fi/cell-tower observations THE DEVICE reports into a position. It needs the device to send those observations — a number alone can never trigger it. Paid.

source: Device intelligence vendors: SEON / Signzy / FingerprintJS
remarks: Vendors that score device/email/phone risk and build a stable device ID across sessions. SEON and FingerprintJS are global; Signzy is India-based. Strengthens the 'same device behind many applicants' (fraud-ring) detection.

source: Credit bureaus: CIBIL / Experian / Equifax / CRIF
what_it_returns: Credit report personal section, historical addresses/phones/employment, enquiry history depending bureau/product.
why_it_matters: One of the richest regulated historical-address sources for lenders.
remarks: India's four RBI-licensed credit bureaus. A lender pulls a report on its OWN applicant using PAN. The report's personal section carries CURRENT and PREVIOUS addresses + phones — one of the richest location sources there is.

input_needed: CKYC ID or permitted identity search via institution
what_it_returns: KYC address and KYC update information available through governed access.
why_it_matters: Independent KYC-address history/reference under regulated institutional access.
remarks: The central government KYC registry (run by CERSAI) where KYC, including address, is stored once and reused. Gives an independent, official address to cross-check the declared one. Access is governed.

input_needed: customer consent token via licensed AA/FIU workflow
what_it_returns: Bank statement data, transaction narrations, salary credits, balances depending consent artefact.
why_it_matters: Can reveal fresh financial behaviour and sometimes merchant/employer geography from transaction text.
remarks: An RBI-regulated 'consent pipe' (via licensed AAs like Finvu, OneMoney, Anumati) that lets a customer share bank-statement data. Transactions reveal where money moves NOW and the salary employer — a fresh, clean, consented location signal.

input_needed: case number or lawful case-linked search
what_it_returns: Case metadata and party details where publicly shown.
why_it_matters: Can support recovery/legal context if case-linked, not a general locator.
remarks: India's public court-records portal. Occasionally surfaces a known address from a person's litigation history. Public, but coarse and to be used carefully and respectfully.

what_it_returns: Delivery PINs/addresses, successful delivery areas, return locations depending partner data.
why_it_matters: Where parcels are actually received can be a strong residence/operations hint.
remarks: Where a person actually receives parcels — a strong 'where they live/operate' signal. Not public; available only through a platform partnership or the customer's consent.

source: People-data enrichment: PeopleDataLabs / Pipl / Clearbit / FullContact
input_needed: email, phone, name, domain, or profile URL
what_it_returns: Merged public/commercial profile data: location, employer, social handles depending vendor.
why_it_matters: Possibility-map only; can add employer/city hints but quality/provenance varies.
remarks: Vendors that take an email/phone/name and return a merged profile (location, employer, social links). Coverage and accuracy vary, so treat results as a lead, not proof. (Clearbit is now part of HubSpot.)

what_it_returns: Crowd-sourced name tags, spam flags, sometimes coarse location text.
why_it_matters: Possible supporting identity/contact hint, not truth.
remarks: Crowd-sourced services (Truecaller is huge in India) that map a number to a name + spam flag and sometimes a coarse city. A supporting identity/location hint, not proof; bound by their terms.

source: Hunter.io / HIBP / Holehe-style email footprint tools
what_it_returns: Domain/account footprint or breach exposure depending tool.
why_it_matters: Mostly identity/footprint, not location. Included only to avoid forgetting the category.
remarks: Tools that show where an email is registered online and whether it appeared in breaches. This is about identity/footprint, NOT location — linked accounts only occasionally hint at a city.

source: Aggregate public social activity by area
input_needed: city/district/hashtag/place query; platform API where allowed
what_it_returns: Area-level post counts or geotagged activity density, not person-level records.
why_it_matters: Regional context only: helps understand active areas, not where a customer is.
remarks: Area-level public post/check-in density (never a named person). Listed for completeness; not a practical signal for this build.

input_needed: user-authenticated login and granted profile scope
what_it_returns: Self-declared profile location/employer if platform allows and user consents.
why_it_matters: Optional low-priority corroboration when customer explicitly provides it.
remarks: If a user logs in and grants access, a platform can share their self-declared city/employer. Weak and only with genuine consent; kept as a possibility.

what_it_returns: Bio/profile city text such as “Bengaluru” or employer/location.
why_it_matters: Only a weak lead; may corroborate business/professional info if lawfully used.
remarks: A city someone writes on a public profile. Weak and risky for a private individual; listed only so the catalogue is complete.

what_it_returns: Unknown stolen records.
why_it_matters: No legitimate use. Listed only so I remember to reject it.
remarks: Stolen records of unknown accuracy that circulate online. Catalogued so it's on the map; not a real, stable, or safe source — and very different from the bank's own dormant-account flags.

source: Live phone tracking / CDR / tower location from mobile number
what_it_returns: Would imply live/current network location if obtained by authorized agencies only.
why_it_matters: Not part of this project.
remarks: There is no public way to get a phone's live tower/network location from just the number; any site claiming this is false/unsafe. CDRs are held by telcos and released only by legal process. Catalogued for awareness.

what_it_returns: Potential electoral registration details.
why_it_matters: Not suitable for bank location-probability work.
remarks: Electoral rolls exist publicly, but repurposing them to trace a person is not a sound source for this work. Catalogued only.

source: Fake accounts / social scraping / friend graph tracking
what_it_returns: Private/profile/network data collected through deception or scraping.
why_it_matters: Not legitimate.
remarks: Collecting someone's profile/network through fake accounts or scraping. Listed for completeness; not part of the build.

source: Data broker dumps / shady people-search OSINT
what_it_returns: Opaque personal profiles, addresses, relatives, social handles.
why_it_matters: Not bank-safe.
remarks: Opaque people-search dumps of unknown provenance. Catalogued for awareness; not a reliable source.

what_it_returns: Identity/location inference from images.
why_it_matters: Not part of project.
remarks: Inferring identity/location from photos. Listed for completeness; out of scope for this build.
